introduction_strategy.hook_hypothesis: AI data centers are a fast-growing, very large grid load; interconnection delays and grid stress motivate treating them as flexible resources.
introduction_strategy.problem_gap_hypothesis: Flexibility of AI inference fleets is usually assumed rather than derived from serving SLOs, and evaluated against price/carbon signals without transmission constraints; it is unknown where such fleets can connect and which signal should steer them (scoped to RTS-GMLC and the Azure 2024 LLM trace).

content_bullets: Problem: AI inference campuses as huge grid loads; flexibility assumed and network ignored.
Method: SLO-grounded linear envelopes from an iteration-level serving simulator driven by Azure 2024 trace; network-constrained DC-OPF on RTS-GMLC; exact flexible-interconnection map; solver study.

Results: shed ~4.9% of load, ~19.8% deferrable energy; LME-following cuts hosting emissions 5.7-12.3% vs 2.4-3.2% cost co-opt; Knittel effect at coal bus 101; 500 MW campus hostable at 48 vs 36 buses, hosting capacity 35.25 -> 42.90 GW (+22%); exact screening 3.2x speed with 0 gap while hard-constraint learners fail.
